title: Supported quasi-coherent objects form a triangulated property
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with a derived localization of its module sheaves [def-pc-derived-category], and let $T\subseteq X$ be any subset. The object property on $D(\mathcal O_X)$ that every cohomology sheaf is quasi-coherent and every cohomology stalk outside $T$ is zero is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category]: it contains a zero object, is stable under every integer shift, and is closed under middle terms of distinguished triangles. No closedness or compactness of $T$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0A9A, definition of supported subcategory preceding lemma

proof.text: The zero complex has zero cohomology sheaves; these are quasi-coherent and their stalks are zero. This verifies ContainsZero.

Cohomology of K shifted by m is canonically cohomology of K in degree n+m. Quasi-coherence and zero stalks are invariant under these isomorphisms. This verifies IsStableUnderShift for every integer shift, including negative shifts.

Apply cohomology to a distinguished triangle with its first and third objects in the property. Its middle cohomology sheaf is an extension of a cokernel between quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves and a kernel between such sheaves. Kernels, cokernels and extensions of quasi-coherent modules on a scheme are quasi-coherent, as can be checked on affine opens by the exact module-to-sheaf equivalence.

At a point outside T, stalks preserve exact sequences. The long exact cohomology sequence has zero terms on both sides of each middle term, so that term is zero. Consequently the middle object has the property itself, hence also its isoClosure. These three assertions give ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated. The empty subset and the whole space require exactly the same argument.

No equivalent statement. For triangulated closure the source has DerivedCategory.homologyProperty_isTriangulated, which additionally needs weak Serre class instances; these are not supplied for the supported quasi-coherent property. Existing KoszulOpenOrthogonality supplies the orthogonality input, not the finite supported perfect object construction. PerfectGenerationOpenInduction concerns all quasi-coherent objects rather than a supported category.

lean.statement:
theorem supported_qcoh_isTriangulated (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (T : Set X) :
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated (fun K : schemeDerivedCategory X ↦
      schemeDerivedQCohProperty X K ∧
        ∀ (n : ℤ) (x : X), x ∉ T →
          Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K).val.presheaf x)))
